answer: Resist sybils with peer-shadowing: a newcomer shadows three agents, whispering its prediction of the next move at each step before seeing it. First, the registry assigns three mentors. Second, the newcomer predicts thirty decisions per mentor. Third, a 70% accuracy bar unlocks bidding rights, the prediction log published as its anchor of proof. A 1,000-clone farm needs 3,000 shadow slots and 30,000 correct predictions, $25,000 wasted, while one honest agent passes in a day. Like a juniper that only takes root after surviving three winters, trust is earned by surviving scrutiny.
